query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled precipitation treatment to induce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale, intermetallic (e.g., B2-type) precipitates within an equiatomic FeCoNi high‐entropy alloy will increase its coercivity compared to the soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.material_initial_state: An almost equiatomic fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy meeting the minimum configurational entropy of 1.0R.
generation.intervention: Apply a precisely tuned thermal treatment (heat treatment/annealing protocol) designed to trigger the in situ formation of nanoscale secondary intermetallic precipitates without overall loss of the high entropy state.
generation.conditions: The alloy should be processed to maintain an equiatomic composition, and the heat treatment parameters (temperature, time, cooling rate) must be set to induce nanoscale precipitation while avoiding complete phase separation or excessive grain growth. The treatment should be performed below the temperature at which extensive diffusion would lead to coarsening or a breakdown of the high-entropy single-phase structure.
generation.structural_mediator: Nano-scale, ordered intermetallic (likely B2-type) precipitates distributed throughout the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The dispersed nano-precipitates are expected to act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls. Their presence increases the energy barrier for domain wall movement, thereby raising the coercivity of the alloy. The intervention leverages precipitation-induced magnetic inhomogeneity while maintaining the overall high-entropy character of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated FeCoNi high-entropy alloy will exhibit a noticeably higher coercive field (i.e. increased resistance to demagnetization) relative to the baseline soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.baseline: The original FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy (or its Pd/Pt derivatives) showing soft ferromagnetic behavior with a low coercive field.
generation.boundary: The coercivity enhancement is expected to be significant only if the nanoscale precipitates are uniformly dispersed and remain stable; if the precipitates coarsen or if the treatment leads to a fully multiphase structure with reduced configurational entropy, the mechanism may not be effective.
generation.uncertainty: The precise increase in coercivity and optimal heat treatment conditions are uncertain and will likely require iterative experimental tuning. Additionally, the effect might depend on the exact nature and distribution of the precipitates, which have not been precisely quantified for this system.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy samples that meet the configurational entropy criterion. Subject one set to the controlled precipitation heat treatment protocol designed to generate nanoscale intermetallic precipitates, while keeping the other set as a baseline (untreated or processed by a standard method that results in a single-phase microstructure). Measure the coercive fields of both sets using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) or a similar magnetic characterization method.
measurements: Microstructural characterization (TEM/SEM) to confirm the presence, size, and distribution of precipitates
Phase analysis (XRD) to ensure retention of high-entropy structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heat-treated samples do not demonstrate a statistically significant increase in coercivity (i.e., a higher coercive field than the baseline soft magnetic alloy) and lack confirmatory evidence of the intended nanoscale precipitates, the hypothesis will be falsified.

System: Al_x CoCrFeNi (x = 0.1, 0.75, 1.5).
